notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Course, school and computing layers were not found at UNM (course layer deferred), so only the five university-layer documents are coded. The syllabus-language page reproduces sample statements from OSU, Temple, UT Tyler, DePaul, Brockport and Ontario Tech; they are coded as models UNM publishes, not as UNM rules. Both coders put the AI-specific lists in the provost memo addendum (permitted, conditional, not permitted uses) as separate units; coder A coded more of those list items than coder B, and all were kept because each is a distinct stated use. Conventions applied in reconciliation: (1) a syllabus-statement duty or recommendation is phase course-start (communicating expectations); (2) UNM's own statements of principle are actor admin/all and phase general; (3) the footnote or attribution statements that disclose UNM's own AI drafting are P84 (how the guidance was made) with a fit_note. In the Academic Integrity Guide, three items with no link to AI (exam devices, citing any source, a second ask-the-professor line; none names AI) were dropped as boilerplate.
